properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js (SHA-1/SHA-2 digest streams) is a real declared dependency in pnpm-lock.yaml, shipped in the app bundle transitively via the crypto-browserify/elliptic/ethers chain behind the wagmi/web3modal/coinbase-wallet stack. No direct call site in first-party code; presence in the shipped dependency tree is what this inventory records. Changeable here by pruning the wallet SDK's transitive deps.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Browser crypto-polyfill dependency of dapp-slaps' SvelteKit frontend: browserify-aes/browserify-cipher/parse-asn1 use evp_bytestokey to emulate node:crypto in the browser bundle via vite-plugin-node-polyfills (packages/app/vite.config.ts). No application source calls it directly; changeable here only by trimming the node polyfills. The legacy single-iteration MD5 EVP_BytesToKey KDF ships in the bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The Ethereum signing curve of this dapp: viem signs/verifies with secp256k1, and wallet connections (MetaMask etc.) authenticate with secp256k1 ECDSA. Quantum-unsafe under Shor, but secp256k1 is EVM consensus — observable here, replaceable only at the ecosystem level; ML-DSA-65 is the eventual successor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: create-ecdh is the ECDH primitive of crypto-browserify, bundled by vite-plugin-node-polyfills (a direct devDependency of packages/app) so wallet-SDK code expecting Node's crypto works in the browser. Classical ECDH shipped in the bundle; no first-party call site. Changeable here by tightening the polyfill config.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 implementation available in the shipped dependency tree: noble-curves 1.1.0 (via @coinbase/wallet-sdk → @solana/web3.js) is the Ed25519 engine for Solana keypairs in the wallet connector; the 1.0.0 path (viem) makes it available to the frontend too. No first-party Ed25519 call site in app source — presence in the shipped library is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Signature engine of the ethers-based wallet-connector stack: secp256k1 ECDSA signs Ethereum transactions and Safe app messages. Quantum-unsafe (Shor); migration ML-DSA-65 is ecosystem-gated for EVM signatures. Also present in the browser node:crypto polyfill via create-ecdh/browserify-sign. No direct call site in app source — the connectors invoke it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 is one of the curves shipped in @noble/curves (1.0.0/1.1.0 in the lockfile), the crypto provider behind viem — the library that actually performs this dapp's secp256k1 signing/verification and hashing. Presence in the shipped bundle is the inventory fact; the app's own calls go through viem's wrappers.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 is the EVM's mandated hash — addresses, transaction hashes, ABI encoding — used by every wallet interaction this dapp makes. Grover gives only a square-root speedup, so not urgent; and it is EVM consensus, not changeable unilaterally here. Changeable: no (ecosystem-gated).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two real PBKDF2 consumers ship in this tree: ethers' BIP39 mnemonic→seed and keystore KDF (HD wallet path of the Safe connector stack), and the browser PBKDF2 of the node:crypto polyfill (which parse-asn1 uses for OpenSSL-style encrypted-key decryption). Quantum-safe KDF; iterations and purpose are set by the callers.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js is the memory-hard KDF of Ethereum's V3 keystore format, pulled into the lockfile by @ethersproject/json-wallets (ethers v5, transitive behind @coinbase/wallet-sdk / web3modal). It protects encrypted key files (e.g. browser wallet keystore imports); quantum relevance is low but it is real password-hashing crypto in the shipped stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF-SHA256 is the middle of WalletConnect's relay crypto: X25519 key agreement → HKDF → ChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption of wallet↔dapp relay messages. The HKDF itself is post-quantum-era; the X25519 feeding it is the harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure (tracked as separate inventory objects). Changeable only by WalletConnect's protocol design; the relay protocol gained a PQ option in v2 later than this pinned stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 as provided by @noble/hashes (1.3.0/1.3.1), the hash library bundled with viem — used for Ethereum hashing paths (block hashes, EIP-712 digests etc.) inside the dapp's RPC stack. Dependency-inventory asset; no direct first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 is part of @noble/hashes@1.3.0's API surface shipped with viem (the app's web3 library) and 1.3.1 with @solana/web3.js. Post-quantum-suitable hash; no first-party call site in app source — presence in the shipped library is the inventory fact, not a defect.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: This is the actively-used Keccak-256 implementation of the frontend: viem calls noble's keccak_256 for EVM hashing (transaction digests, address computation, EIP-712 typed data). Same EVM-consensus caveat as the other Keccak entries — not changeable unilaterally.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The hashing core of this dapp's web3 stack: @noble/hashes provides the SHA-2/SHA-3/Keccak/BLAKE/RIPEMD primitives that viem and @scure use for Ethereum hashing and BIP32/BIP39 key derivation. The pinned version (1.3.0/1.3.1) decides the shipped crypto surface; available in the browser bundle whether or not app code calls it directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves is the elliptic-curve crypto provider of the whole dapp: viem (direct devDependency of packages/app) uses it for secp256k1 ECDSA signing/verification and key handling, and it also ships P-256, Ed25519, X25519 etc. The bundle exposes these algorithms whether or not first-party code calls them directly. Changeable here by bumping viem/@noble/curves versions.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js is the scrypt KDF behind Ethereum JSON keystore (EIP-2335-style) wallet encryption in the ethers stack pulled by the Safe/wagmi connectors — memory-hard key derivation for wallet files. No first-party call site; the connector code path uses it when importing/decrypting keystore wallets.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js@2.4.11 provides SHA-1/SHA-2 stream implementations; it is the digest engine behind create-hash/create-hmac (crypto-browserify) and elliptic's hashing in the browserified bundle. Real crypto provider shipped with the app; no direct first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: EC crypto library in the shipped bundle: elliptic implements secp256k1 ECDSA/ECDH behind ethers' signing-key (Ethereum transaction signing in the Safe/wagmi connector stack) and behind the browser node:crypto polyfill's create-ecdh/browserify-sign. Quantum-unsafe EC algorithms available in the library, present in the bundle whether or not app code calls them directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js supplies the SHA-256/SHA-512 behind ethers' sha2 module — used for BIP32 HD key derivation (HMAC-SHA512) and message digests in the ethers-based wallet connectors. Present in the shipped dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The browser PBKDF2 of the node:crypto polyfill injected into the client bundle by vite-plugin-node-polyfills; parse-asn1 uses it to decrypt OpenSSL-formatted (EVP_BytesToKey-derived) encrypted private keys. Real crypto surface in the shipped bundle; no direct application call site.
